spec.full_target: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer lambda with 0 <= lambda < p, and admissible lattice M in V(lambda), the L(K)-module M tensor_Z K is irreducible.
spec.conclusion: M tensor_Z K is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

parameters.type: admissible lattice in V(lambda) over Z

hypotheses.origin: Exercise context: K is any field of positive characteristic p.

hypotheses.statement: K is a field of characteristic p.
lambda is an integer and 0 <= lambda < p.

M is an arbitrary admissible lattice in the characteristic-zero irreducible highest-weight module V(lambda): M is free abelian of rank lambda+1, its Z-basis is a C-basis of V(lambda), and U_Z M is contained in M.
hypotheses.origin: Exercise context, sections 27.1 and 27.4; arbitrary-lattice convention explicitly fixed in source-context.md.

calculations: Finite matrix multiplication and binomial coefficient identities; localization and tensor product calculations over Z and Z_(p); elementary finite-module calculations over the PID Z_(p).

primitives.meaning: The complex field used for the characteristic-zero module and the lattice M.

primitives.type: localization of Z at the prime ideal (p)
primitives.meaning: The subring of Q consisting of fractions a/b with p not dividing b.
The Z-subalgebra of the enveloping algebra generated by divided powers X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for r >= 0.
The scalar extension of the Z-span of x,y,h with [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h, acting on M tensor_Z K.

propositions.statement: K is a field of characteristic p.
lambda is an integer and 0 <= lambda < p.
M is a free abelian subgroup of V(lambda), of rank lambda+1, whose Z-basis is a C-basis of V(lambda), and U_Z M is contained in M.
The K-vector space M tensor_Z K is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under x,y,h is either zero or M tensor_Z K.

argument.text: Let n=lambda+1 and take the standard complex basis e_i=y^i v_+/i! for 0<=i<=lambda. The divided-power actions are X_r e_i=binom(lambda-i+r,r)e_(i-r) and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r), with out-of-range basis vectors interpreted as zero. These follow by repeated use of the sl2 relations and the highest-weight equations. Thus their matrices in this basis are integral. Put R=Z_(p), M_R=R tensor_Z M inside V(lambda), and A_R equal to the image of U_Z tensor_Z R acting on V(lambda). Admissibility gives A_R M_R subset M_R.

Write E_ab for the complex-linear operator sending e_b to e_a and every other basis vector to zero. Directly from the formulas, Y_lambda X_lambda=E_lambda,lambda; X_(lambda-i) E_lambda,lambda=E_i,lambda; and E_lambda,lambda Y_(lambda-j)=binom(lambda,j)E_lambda,j. Each binom(lambda,j) is a unit of R because 0<=lambda<p. Therefore E_lambda,j belongs to A_R, and E_i,j=E_i,lambda E_lambda,j belongs to A_R for all i,j. For lambda=0 these formulas give the identity operator as the sole matrix unit. Since these operators are in A_R and preserve M_R, all E_i,j preserve M_R.

For each i let J_i={c in C: c e_i is in M_R}. The projection E_i,i maps the finitely generated R-module M_R onto J_i e_i, so J_i is finitely generated over R. It is nonzero since M_R spans V(lambda) over C and E_i,i is a nonzero projection. Applying E_i,j to c e_j proves J_j subset J_i, and E_j,i proves equality. Write their common value J. The coordinate projections show M_R=direct_sum_{i=0}^lambda J e_i: one inclusion follows by projecting each m in M_R; the other follows from the definition of J. Since M_R is free of rank n over R, tensoring this decomposition with the fraction field Q of R gives n= n dim_Q(J tensor_R Q), so J has rank one. J is torsion-free because it is an R-submodule of C. Here is the elementary rank-one finite-module argument: choose a Q-linear identification J tensor_R Q with Q; the image of J is a finitely generated R-submodule of Q, hence a fractional ideal. Multiplying by a common denominator makes it an ideal of R. The ring R=Z_(p) is a PID, so that nonzero ideal is principal, and J is free of rank one. Consequently J/pJ is one-dimensional over F_p. The decomposition identifies M_R/pM_R with the standard module over F_p on the images of e_0,...,e_lambda, with the divided-power matrices above reduced modulo p.

Localization and reduction identify M_R/pM_R with M tensor_Z F_p: on a Z-basis of M both are the vector space with the same basis and the same reduced integral action matrices. Extending scalars along F_p to K identifies M tensor_Z K with the standard reduced module. This is an isomorphism of L(K)-modules, not merely of vector spaces.

In the standard reduced module, for every r<=lambda<p, X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! are scalar multiples of compositions of x and y, since r! is invertible in F_p. The displayed matrix-unit identities therefore show that the algebra generated by the actions of x and y contains every E_i,j, also when p=2. If a submodule W contains a nonzero vector sum_i c_i e_i, choose i with c_i nonzero. For every j, E_j,i sends that vector to c_i e_j, so scalar closure gives e_j in W. Hence W is the whole module. The module is nonzero because its dimension is lambda+1>=1. This proves the target, including lambda=0.
